GLM-5.3-Flash pools index keys before selecting attention tokens. Add forward APIs for gated cache updates, paged scoring, pool selection, and causal token-ID expansion on Blackwell SM100/SM103.

**The standalone frontend scorer is not yet performant.**
 Large prefill through `pooled_indexer_forward` is 10.7–11.7× slower than DeepGEMM plus the same selector. The serving integration keeps DeepGEMM. The measured cuDNN improvement comes from `pooled_select_forward`, which fuses selection and expansion and accepts native BF16 logits. The vLLM branch also improves prefill cache writes; reported E2E gains cover both changes. No selector-only E2E ablation was measured.

The [vLLM integration](https://github.com/Anerudhan/vllm/tree/feat/glm5next-pooled-dsa-fusion) calls the public `cudnn.ops.dsa.pooled_select_forward` API and `pooled_select_workspace_size`. Selection consumes native BF16 DeepGEMM logits and fuses top-k, token expansion, incomplete-pool tails, and padding into one CuTe DSL launch. Prefill and decode use separate kernels. vLLM retains DeepGEMM scoring, its cache format, and its Triton cache writer. It imports no private frontend helper.

The other public functions are `pooled_indexer_forward`, `pooled_cache_update_forward`, and `pooled_expand_forward`. They provide a standalone full indexer, cache update, and expansion path. The full indexer accepts BF16 weights, uses the SM100 DeepGEMM BF16 head-reduction order, and materializes BF16 logits. 

FP32 weights retain the FP32 path. FP8/FP4 reads accept packed UE8M0 query scales; FP4 also accepts signed packed bytes. Setting `fp8_scale_format="ue8m0"` on the indexer and cache writer uses native vLLM FP8 cache encoding. Existing callers retain the default FP32 scale encoding. The indexer launches scoring followed by fused selection/expansion; an optional cache update adds one launch. 

The vLLM adapter does not call the full indexer.

All functions support caller-owned buffers and explicit CUDA streams. With output and workspace supplied, selection allocates no device storage, copies or converts no tensors, reads no device values on the host, and does not synchronize. It validates shapes, dtypes, strides, alignment, device placement, and writable-buffer overlap. Compilation is reused within the declared capacity. The APIs require CuTe DSL 4.8 or later; validation uses 4.8.0. Backward and autograd are not implemented.

See [the API contract and usage](https://github.com/Anerudhan/cudnn-frontend/blob/feat/pooled-dsa-blackwell/docs/fe-oss-apis/pooled_dsa.md#selection-from-logits).

Validation:

- `cd test/python && "$venv/bin/python" -m pytest -o addopts= -q deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_pooled_dsa.py`: **112 passed** on GB200 and **112 passed** on GB300, using the rebuilt frontend on develop `6fcc0aa59107d9ff690f30934ab936a9ad01a3b9`.
- Coverage includes BF16/FP32 logits, pool sizes 4/16, causal boundaries, ties, padded rows/strides, buffer rejection, explicit streams, allocation/synchronization guards, and changed-input CUDA graph replay.
- Direct comparison against DeepGEMM checks 346,823,998 valid scores per GPU across 12 FP8/FP4 decode and prefill cases, including 4096 queries and 32768 pools. All checked scores and selected-score multisets match exactly. Final jobs: GB200 3482566, GB300 3482567.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.

- The public `cudnn.ops.dsa` export index matches all six names. All 10 API-index fixture tests pass.

Performance was measured on 2026-10-26 against vLLM main `70d67f19dcf822b97b5f8863b7590edd73a59b23`. The frontend runtime is `dfd51c2f645746219aa7c102b2471f62c2038b85`; the standalone indexer changes are validated separately and are not used by this serving measurement. The vLLM branch uses the public API plus direct prefill cache input, so the gain covers that combined change. DeepGEMM scoring remains in use.

GLM-5.3-Flash uses the saved checkpoint `eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`, TP=4, FP8 weights/KV, BF16 compute, 64K context capacity, and 4096-token prefill chunks. Both variants use fixed CPU affinity, identical MoE tuning files, and both server orders. There are six samples per workload and variant. All 1536 timed requests completed with the requested 128 output tokens and no failures. Each server is profiled after timing.

| Input | Concurrency | GB200 output token/s: upstream → API | Gain | GB300 output token/s: upstream → API | Gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K | 1 | 158.46 → 160.90 | +1.5% | 157.74 → 160.24 | +1.6% |
| 4K | 8 | 459.25 → 473.73 | +3.2% | 463.74 → 475.17 | +2.5% |
| 16K | 1 | 100.59 → 102.29 | +1.7% | 100.75 → 101.71 | +1.0% |
| 16K | 8 | 170.48 → 175.84 | +3.1% | 170.48 → 175.06 | +2.7% |
| 32K | 1 | 67.23 → 68.76 | +2.3% | 67.11 → 68.52 | +2.1% |

GB200 TTFT rises 4.3% for 16K/concurrency 8 despite higher output throughput. The paired 32-token smoke continuations match in 7/8 GB200 checks and 8/8 GB300 checks. Every smoke prompt returns its expected answer. One GB200 continuation differs after nine tokens; strict model-output equivalence and full model quality have not been established. The selection contract permits different pool IDs when scores tie.

`SparseAttnIndexerKpool.forward_native` microbenchmarks include API dispatch and validation in eager timing. Each GPU runs 30 FP8/MXFP4 read and FP8 write cases, plus 12 FP8 serving shapes, in both orders. Selected-score multisets and causal token/pool/tail checks pass for every case. Native BF16 cache and MXFP4 insertion have no native comparison.

| GPU | Full matrix eager speedup | Full matrix CUDA graph speedup | Serving-shape CUDA graph speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GB200 | 1.18–1.54× | 1.06–1.56× | 1.14–1.96× |
| GB300 | 1.19–1.54× | 1.05–1.55× | 1.11–1.93× |

The 30-case graph matrix improves in all 60 order-specific comparisons per GPU. Runtime Python hashes match the recorded commits, and all ten compiled vLLM libraries match between variants.

GLM-5.3-Flash pools index keys before selecting attention tokens. Add forward APIs for gated cache updates, paged scoring, pool selection, and causal token-ID expansion on Blackwell SM100/SM103.

**The standalone frontend scorer is not yet performant.**
 Large prefill through `pooled_indexer_forward` is 10.7–11.7× slower than DeepGEMM plus the same selector. The serving integration keeps DeepGEMM. The measured cuDNN improvement comes from `pooled_select_forward`, which fuses selection and expansion and accepts native BF16 logits. The vLLM branch also improves prefill cache writes; reported E2E gains cover both changes. No selector-only E2E ablation was measured.

The [vLLM integration](https://github.com/Anerudhan/vllm/tree/feat/glm5next-pooled-dsa-fusion) calls the public `cudnn.ops.dsa.pooled_select_forward` API and `pooled_select_workspace_size`. Selection consumes native BF16 DeepGEMM logits and fuses top-k, token expansion, incomplete-pool tails, and padding into one CuTe DSL launch. Prefill and decode use separate kernels. vLLM retains DeepGEMM scoring, its cache format, and its Triton cache writer. It imports no private frontend helper.

The other public functions are `pooled_indexer_forward`, `pooled_cache_update_forward`, and `pooled_expand_forward`. They provide a standalone full indexer, cache update, and expansion path. The full indexer accepts BF16 weights, uses the SM100 DeepGEMM BF16 head-reduction order, and materializes BF16 logits.

+"""Compare prepared pooled DSA components with the matching vLLM stages.
+
+This does not measure forward_native or score/top-k kernels. Inputs and
+compilation are outside timing. Repeated calls reuse warm caches and fixed
+metadata. FP8 cache writes and index expansion have optional vLLM baselines;
+BF16 and MXFP4 cache writers have no upstream native baseline.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import socket
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def measure(torch, fn, warmup, repeats, iterations):
+    for _ in range(warmup):
+        fn()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    wall, span = [], []
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        start.record()
+        before = time.perf_counter()
+        for _ in range(iterations):
+            fn()
+        end.record()
+        end.synchronize()
+        wall.append((time.perf_counter() - before) * 1e6 / iterations)
+        span.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / iterations)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        for _ in range(iterations):
+            fn()
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    replay = []
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        start.record()
+        graph.replay()
+        end.record()
+        end.synchronize()
+        replay.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / iterations)
+    return {
+        "wall_us": statistics.median(wall),
+        "cuda_span_us": statistics.median(span),
+        "graph_us": statistics.median(replay),
+        "wall_samples_us": wall,
+        "cuda_span_samples_us": span,
+        "graph_samples_us": replay,
+    }
+
+
+def expansion_case(torch, pooled, rows, pool_size, phase, baseline):
+    ids = torch.arange(512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).repeat(rows, 1)
+    positions = torch.full((rows,), 32768 + phase - 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+    output = torch.empty(rows, 512 * pool_size + pool_size - 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    plan = pooled.ExpandIndices(ids, positions, output, pool_size)
+    plan.compile()
+    fn = lambda: plan.execute(ids, positions, output)
+    fn()
+    expected = torch.full_like(output, -1)
+    expected[:, : 512 * pool_size] = torch.arange(512 * pool_size, device="cuda")
+    tail = phase % pool_size
+    if tail:
+        expected[:, 512 * pool_size : 512 * pool_size + tail] = torch.arange(32768, 32768 + tail, device="cuda")
+    torch.testing.assert_close(output, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    methods = {"cudnn_expand": fn}
+    if baseline:
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops import kpool_compress as ops
+
+        reference_out = torch.empty_like(output)
+
+        def upstream():
+            reference_out.fill_(-1)
+            expanded = ops.expand_pools_and_append_tail(ids.to(torch.int64), positions.to(torch.int32) + 1, pool_size)
+            reference_out.copy_(expanded)
+
+        upstream()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(reference_out, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        methods["vllm_expand_stage"] = upstream
+    return methods
+
+
+def cache_case(torch, pooled, rows, pool_size, phase, dtype, mode, baseline):
+    page_size = 64
+    requests = 1 if mode == "prefill" else rows
+    width = page_size * {"bf16": 256, "fp8": 132, "fp4": 68}[dtype]
+    pages_per_request = (rows // pool_size + page_size - 1) // page_size if mode == "prefill" else 1
+    pages_per_request = max(pages_per_request, 1)
+    keys = torch.randn(rows, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    gates = torch.zeros_like(keys)
+    ape = torch.zeros(pool_size, 128, device="cuda")
+    cache = torch.zeros(requests * pages_per_request, width, device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+    tail = torch.randn(requests, 2, pool_size, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    tail[:, 1].zero_()
+    positions = (
+        torch.arange(rows, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64) if mode == "prefill" else torch.full((rows,), 32768 + phase - 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+    )
+    request_ids = torch.zeros(rows, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64) if mode == "prefill" else torch.arange(rows, device="cuda")
+    logical = positions // pool_size if mode == "prefill" else torch.zeros_like(positions)
+    slots = torch.where((positions + 1) % pool_size == 0, request_ids * pages_per_request * page_size + logical, -1)
+    tail_slots = request_ids * pool_size + positions % pool_size
+    cu = torch.tensor([0, rows], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32) if mode == "prefill" else torch.arange(rows + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    args = (keys, gates, ape, cache, tail, slots, tail_slots, positions if mode == "decode" else None, cu if mode == "decode" else None)
+    plan = pooled.PoolCacheUpdate(*args, pool_size=pool_size, page_size=page_size, cache_dtype=dtype, mode=mode)
+    plan.compile()
+    methods = {"cudnn_cache": lambda: plan.execute(*args)}
+    initial_cache, initial_tail = cache.clone(), tail.clone()
+    methods["cudnn_cache"]()
+    if baseline and dtype == "fp8":
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia import sparse_indexer
+        from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops import kpool_compress as ops
+
+        reference_cache = initial_cache.clone().view(-1, page_size, 132)
+        reference_tail = initial_tail.clone()
+
+        def upstream():
+            if mode == "prefill":
+                sparse_indexer._kpool_compress_insert(keys, gates, ape, reference_cache, slots, pool_size, 128, True)
+                ops.kpool_seed_tail_cache(reference_tail, keys, gates, tail_slots, pool_size, 128)
+            else:

+                    reference_tail,
+                    tail_slots.view(rows, 1),
+                    keys.view(rows, 1, 128),
+                    gates.view(rows, 1, 128),
+                    ape,
+                    slots.view(rows, 1),
+                    positions.to(torch.int32).view(rows, 1),
+                    pool_size,

+                    True,
+                )

+        upstream()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(reference_cache.flatten(1), cache, rtol=0, atol=0)

+        methods["vllm_cache_stage"] = upstream
+    # Check cache state with the full numerical pytest suite before timing.
+    # This harness checks shared FP8 paths exactly; it does not certify new dtypes.
+    cache.copy_(initial_cache)
+    tail.copy_(initial_tail)
+    return methods
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--rows", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 64, 1024])
+    parser.add_argument("--dtypes", nargs="+", choices=["bf16", "fp8", "fp4"], default=["bf16", "fp8", "fp4"])
+    parser.add_argument("--pool-size", type=int, choices=[4, 16], default=4)
+    parser.add_argument("--phases", type=int, nargs="+", help="Causal length modulo pool size; pool size means a complete pool")
+    parser.add_argument("--with-vllm", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--check-only", action="store_true", help="Run comparisons without performance measurements")
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=20)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=15)
+    parser.add_argument("--iterations", type=int, default=10)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("pooled-components.json"))
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    phases = args.phases or list(range(1, args.pool_size + 1))
+    if min(args.rows + [args.warmup, args.repeats, args.iterations]) < 1 or any(p < 1 or p > args.pool_size for p in phases):
+        parser.error("rows/timing counts must be positive and phases must be in [1, pool_size]")
+    hostname = socket.gethostname()
+    import torch
+    import cudnn
+    from cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention import pooled
+
+    torch.manual_seed(53)
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3)):
+        parser.error("Blackwell SM100 or SM103 is required")
+    data = {
+        "host": hostname,
+        "torch": torch.__version__,
+        "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+        "cudnn_source": cudnn.__file__,
+        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+        "scope": "component stages only; no score/top-k or forward_native",
+        "options": {**vars(args), "output": str(args.output)},
+        "results": [],
+    }
+    if args.with_vllm:
+        import vllm
+
+        data["vllm_source"] = vllm.__file__
+    data["gpu_state"] = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
+
+    def run(kind, rows, phase, dtype, mode, methods):
+        for method, fn in methods.items():
+            result = {"component": kind, "rows": rows, "phase": phase, "dtype": dtype, "mode": mode, "method": method}
+            if not args.check_only:
+                result.update(measure(torch, fn, args.warmup, args.repeats, args.iterations))
+            data["results"].append(result)
+            args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            args.output.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n")

+            run("expand", rows, phase, "int32", "both", expansion_case(torch, pooled, rows, args.pool_size, phase, args.with_vllm))

+# Pooled DSA
+
+Pooled DSA selects groups of index keys, then expands each selected group to
+individual token IDs. `cudnn.ops.dsa` provides a pooled indexer and separate
+selection, cache-update, and index-expansion APIs for Blackwell SM100/SM103.
+
+## Performance status
+
+**The standalone frontend scorer is not yet performant.** Use the public
+selector with DeepGEMM logits for the measured vLLM serving route.
+`pooled_indexer_forward` matches the native BF16 contract on tested inputs,
+but its large-prefill scoring path is much slower than DeepGEMM.
+
+At 4,096 queries, 32,768 pools, 32 heads, and head dimension 128, CUDA-graph
+stage measurements on exclusive GB200/GB300 nodes give:
+
+| GPU | Cache | DeepGEMM score ms | Frontend score ms | Shared selector ms | Full-indexer slowdown |
+| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| GB200 | FP8 | 0.376 | 7.126 | 0.305 | 10.74× |
+| GB200 | FP4 | 0.283 | 6.612 | 0.305 | 11.61× |
+| GB300 | FP8 | 0.343 | 7.089 | 0.303 | 11.59× |
+| GB300 | FP4 | 0.283 | 6.579 | 0.304 | 11.73× |
+
+Each value averages medians from both execution orders, with 15 samples
+per order and ten calls per graph after warmup. The full-indexer ratio
+includes scoring and the same fused selector in both paths. Native prefill
+K gathering is excluded; the frontend reads paged keys directly. These
+measurements use frontend `13892e8e625a4a8445e1a1be031046b4b84018cf`.
+
+The cuDNN contribution to the measured GLM-5.3-Flash serving gain comes
+from `pooled_select_forward`: fused selection/expansion and direct BF16
+logit input. The vLLM branch also removes temporary gathers from prefill
+cache writes, so its E2E gains cover both changes. There is no selector-only
+E2E ablation. The full frontend scorer and cache-update API are not used
+by that serving path.
+
+## Selection from logits
+
+`cudnn.ops.dsa.pooled_select_forward` accepts precomputed BF16 or FP32
+indexer logits. It selects complete causal pools, expands them into token
+IDs, appends incomplete-pool tail tokens, and fills padding with `-1` in
+one CuTe DSL launch. It has separate prefill and decode kernels. It performs
+no scoring, pooling, quantization, or attention softmax.
+
+This is the API used by the vLLM pooled-selection adapter. DeepGEMM supplies
+native BF16 logits; vLLM retains its existing pooled-key cache format.
+
+```python
+from cudnn.ops import dsa
+
+size = dsa.pooled_select_workspace_size(logits, max_pools=32768)
+workspace = torch.empty(size, dtype=torch.uint8, device=logits.device)
+result = dsa.pooled_select_forward(
+    logits, positions, selected_pools=512, pool_size=4,
+    mode="prefill", max_pools=32768,
+    output=output, workspace=workspace, current_stream=stream)
+indices = result["indices"]
+```
+
+| Argument | Contract |
+|---|---|
+| `logits` | BF16/FP32 `(N,C)`, contiguous columns, positive non-overlapping row stride, 32-byte-aligned address |
+| `positions` | INT32/INT64 `(N,)`, zero-based token positions; positive vector stride |
+| `selected_pools` | Multiple of 32, from 32 to 2048; default 512 |
+| `pool_size` | 4 or 16; default 4 |
+| `mode` | `"decode"` or `"prefill"` |
+| `max_pools` | Compile capacity, `C <= max_pools <= 32768`; defaults to `C` |
+| `output` | Optional INT32 matrix, at least `N` rows and `selected_pools * pool_size + pool_size - 1` columns |
+| `workspace` | Optional contiguous UINT8 vector, aligned to 256 bytes, sized with `pooled_select_workspace_size` |
+| `current_stream` | Optional CUDA stream handle or torch stream; defaults to the current stream |
+
+For position `p`, eligible columns are below
+`min(C, floor((p + 1) / pool_size))`. Negative positions and positions at or
+above `2**31 - 1` produce inactive rows. If the causal context fits within
+`selected_pools * pool_size` tokens, the output contains all causal token IDs
+in ascending order. Otherwise, selected pools occupy the fixed history
+region and up to `pool_size - 1` tail tokens follow it. Extra rows and columns
+are filled with `-1`. Tied IDs and selection order are unspecified. Eligible
+logits must not contain NaNs. The caller supplies columns for the history it
+wants ranked; the operation does not access a cache or page table.
+
+All tensors must share a CUDA device and require no autograd. Output rows
+may be padded, with contiguous columns and a positive non-overlapping row
+stride. Output and workspace must not overlap each other or either input.
+The int32 addressing limit requires `2*N*C < 2**31`.
+
+The workspace query reads only tensor metadata. BF16 specializations whose
+`max_pools` rounds up to 8192, 16384, or 32768 use 32 bytes. Other
+specializations use `8*N*C` bytes. The workspace contains selector scratch;
+it excludes input logits and output storage.
+
+With output and workspace supplied, the API allocates no device storage,
+copies or converts no tensors, reads no device values on the host, and does
+not synchronize. It reuses compilation across changing row counts, columns,
+and supported strides within `max_pools`. Warm up before CUDA graph capture.
+The caller keeps buffers live until execution completes on the chosen
+stream. When buffers are omitted, the function allocates them on that stream.
+It returns `TupleDict(indices=output)`. Backward and autograd are unsupported.
+
+`_compile_pooled_select` remains an internal compiler helper. Applications
+should use the public selection and workspace-size functions above.
+
+## Indexer forward
+
+`pooled_indexer_forward` reads paged pooled keys, scores complete causal pools,
+selects top-k pools, and expands them into token IDs. Optional cache updates
+run first. Inputs begin after Q/K projection; Q rotation and quantization
+remain upstream. Final sparse attention over token K/V is a separate operation.
+
+The real-valued score for query `i` and pool `j` is
+`sum_h weights[i,h] * max(dot(q[i,h], pooled_key[j]), 0)`.
+Only `j < floor((positions[i] + 1) / pool_size)` is eligible. Pool selection
+uses these index scores; it does not apply attention softmax.
+
+BF16 weights select the SM100 DeepGEMM arithmetic contract: tensor-core
+dot products accumulate in FP32, each ReLU result rounds to BF16, and four
+BF16 fused multiply-add chains reduce heads `0,4,...`, `1,5,...`,
+`2,6,...`, and `3,7,...`. BF16 adds combine chains 0+2, 1+3, then the
+two results. The materialized logits are BF16. This is not equivalent to
+rounding an FP32 weighted sum once at the end.
+

+## Pool cache update
+
+`cudnn.ops.dsa.pooled_cache_update_forward` combines gated pooling, normalized
+Hadamard-128, quantization, paged storage, and tail-cache updates in one
+CuTe DSL launch. It needs Blackwell SM100 or SM103 and CuTe DSL 4.8 or later.

+| Argument | Dtype and shape | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|
+| `keys`, `gates` | BF16 `(tokens, 128)` | Raw index keys and channel gates |
+| `ape` | FP32 `(pool_size, 128)` | Learned position bias within a pool |
+| `cache` | UINT8 `(pages, page_bytes)` | Caller-owned pooled-key cache |
+| `tail` | BF16 `(requests, 2, pool_size, 128)` | Per-request K/gate ring; axis 1 selects K or gate |

+| `tail_slots` | INT32/INT64 `(tokens,)` | Physical ring slot `request * pool_size + phase` |
+| `positions` | INT32/INT64 `(tokens,)`, decode only | Absolute zero-based token position |
+| `cu_seqlens` | INT32 `(requests + 1,)`, decode only | Offsets of packed query tokens |

+pool's tokens. It forms the weighted sum of K, rounds to BF16, applies
+Hadamard-128 divided by `sqrt(128)`, then rounds to BF16 again. The cache
+stores this rotated key in the selected format:

+| `cache_dtype` | Bytes per page of `P` pools | Page contents |
+|---|---:|---|
+| `bf16` | `P * 256` | `P` contiguous BF16 vectors |
+| `fp8`, `fp8_scale_format="fp32"` | `P * 132` | `P * 128` E4M3 bytes, then `P` FP32 scales |
+| `fp8`, `fp8_scale_format="ue8m0"` | `P * 132` | Same values, then four repeated UE8M0 bytes per pool, as in native vLLM |
+| `fp4` | `P * 68` | `P * 64` packed E2M1 bytes, then four UE8M0 scales per pool |

+FP8 uses one power-of-two scale per 128 channels. MXFP4 uses one per
+32 channels; the earlier channel occupies the low nibble. FP4 rounds
+to nearest even. All cache formats receive BF16 keys and gates.
+There is no global FP4 scale.

+`"ue8m0"` on both APIs to share a cache with SM100 DeepGEMM. Encoding
+happens in the pooling kernel; no scale conversion kernel is launched.
+
+`mode="prefill"` requires each request's new tokens to start on a pool
+boundary. The kernel reads completed pools directly from packed inputs.
+It copies only the last write to each ring slot. Partial-pool continuation
+must use `mode="decode"`, which processes each request's packed tokens in
+order and combines them with the existing ring. An empty request is allowed.
+
+The caller must provide finite inputs, valid ring contents for prior tokens,
+monotonic decode offsets starting at zero and ending at `tokens`, and unique
+cache ownership per request. Pool slots must identify only complete groups.
+Decode tail-slot phase must equal `position % pool_size`. Negative tail
+slots or positions disable decode rows; negative pool slots disable cache
+writes. The kernel bounds-checks physical cache and tail slots.

+columns and tail token vectors are contiguous. Row/page padding and padding
+between the tail's K/gate blocks are supported. Cache page stride and tensor
+addresses must be four-byte aligned. Writable caches cannot overlap each
+other or any input. Metadata values remain on the device; the caller is
+responsible for the offset and ownership contracts above.
+
+```python
+from cudnn.ops import dsa
+
+result = dsa.pooled_cache_update_forward(
+    keys, gates, ape, cache, tail, pool_slots, tail_slots,
+    positions, cu_seqlens, pool_size=4, page_size=64,
+    cache_dtype="fp8", mode="decode", current_stream=stream)
+```
+
+Workspace size is zero. The function performs no device allocation, host read,
+copy, or synchronization. Token/request/page counts and accepted strides
+may change without recompilation. Pool size, page size, dtypes, mode, and
+device form the compilation-cache key. Warm up before graph capture and keep the
+buffers live until execution completes.
+
+The function returns
+`TupleDict(cache=cache, tail=tail)`. Both outputs are caller-owned state;
+the function does not create or initialize them. No autograd contract is
+provided.
+
+## Index expansion
+
+`cudnn.ops.dsa.pooled_expand_forward` writes a caller-owned INT32 matrix in one
+CuTe DSL launch. It accepts INT32 or INT64 pool IDs and token positions.
+It needs Blackwell SM100 or SM103 and CuTe DSL 4.8 or later.
+
+| Argument | Shape | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|
+| `pool_ids` | `(source_rows, selected_pools)` | Local IDs from top-k; negative IDs are padding |
+| `positions` | `(query_rows,)` | Zero-based token positions; negative values mark inactive rows |
+| `output` | `(output_rows, width)` | Caller-owned INT32 token IDs |
+| `row_map` | `(query_rows,)`, optional INT32 | Output row to source row; negative or out-of-range values mark inactive rows |
+
+All tensors must be on the same CUDA device. Pool sizes 4 and 16 are supported.
+Matrix columns must be contiguous; positive row and vector strides are
+supported. Output must not overlap an input. Positions must be below
+`2**31 - 1`. The result uses local token IDs and `-1` for unused entries.
+
+`output_rows >= query_rows` and
+`width >= selected_pools * pool_size + pool_size - 1` are required. Every
+output element is written, including padded rows and columns.
+
+For a token position `p`, completed pools cover
+`floor((p + 1) / pool_size) * pool_size` tokens. Each selected completed pool
+expands into consecutive token IDs. Up to `pool_size - 1` trailing causal
+tokens follow the fixed history region. Future pool IDs are masked. If the
+whole causal context fits in the history region, the result contains every
+causal token in ascending order.
+
+```python
+from cudnn.ops import dsa
+
+result = dsa.pooled_expand_forward(
+    pool_ids, positions, pool_size=4, output=output, current_stream=stream)
+```
+
+With caller-provided output, the function performs no device allocation,
+conversion, host read, or
+synchronization. Its workspace size is zero. Row counts, selected-pool
+counts, and accepted strides may change without recompilation. Dtypes,
+pool size, device, and the presence of `row_map` form the compilation-cache key.
+Warm up before capture; caller-owned inputs and output must remain live
+until the launch completes.
+
+The function allocates the output when omitted and returns a
+`TupleDict` with the single key `indices`:
+
+```python
+result = dsa.pooled_expand_forward(pool_ids, positions, pool_size=4)
+indices = result["indices"]
+```
+
+The pool selection and token expansion contract follows GLM's
+[`SparseAttnIndexerKpool`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc162b3f9280c2dc05dfd5aa282d29551f8f6d33/vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/sparse_indexer.py).
+`ExpandIndices` receives already selected pools. `PoolCacheUpdate` only
+updates caches. `IndexerForward` combines both with scoring and top-k;
+none of these APIs performs final sparse attention.

+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def cudnn_pooled_scores(
+    Q,
+    QSCALE,
+    WEIGHTS,
+    CACHE,
+    BLOCK_TABLE,
+    CU_QUERY,
+    POSITIONS,
+    SCORES,
+    N_QUERY,
+    N_PAGES,
+    SCORE_COLS,
+    TABLE_COLS,
+    Q_ROW,
+    Q_HEAD,
+    QS_ROW,
+    QS_HEAD,
+    W_ROW,
+    CACHE_PAGE,
+    TABLE_ROW,
+    CU_STRIDE,
+    POS_STRIDE,
+    SCORE_ROW,
+    POOL_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    PAGE_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
+    QUERY_TILE: tl.constexpr,
+    POOL_TILE: tl.constexpr,
+    BF16_REDUCTION: tl.constexpr,
+    FP8_SCALE_FORMAT: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    request = tl.program_id(2)
+    start = tl.load(CU_QUERY + request * CU_STRIDE).to(tl.int64)
+    end = tl.load(CU_QUERY + (request + 1) * CU_STRIDE).to(tl.int64)
+    query_start = start + tl.program_id(1) * QUERY_TILE
+    if query_start < end:
+        m = tl.arange(0, QUERY_TILE * 32)
+        query = query_start + m // 32
+        head = m % 32
+        query_valid = (query >= 0) & (query < end) & (query < N_QUERY)
+        pool = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * POOL_TILE + tl.arange(0, POOL_TILE)
+        page = tl.load(
+            BLOCK_TABLE + request * TABLE_ROW + pool // PAGE_SIZE,
+            (pool < SCORE_COLS) & (pool // PAGE_SIZE < TABLE_COLS),
+            other=-1,
+        ).to(tl.int64)
+        pool_valid = (pool < SCORE_COLS) & (page >= 0) & (page < N_PAGES)
+        page_base = page * CACHE_PAGE
+        slot = pool % PAGE_SIZE
+        if DTYPE == "fp4" or (DTYPE == "fp8" and FP8_SCALE_FORMAT == "ue8m0"):
+            WIDTH: tl.constexpr = 64 if DTYPE == "fp4" else 128
+            FORMAT: tl.constexpr = "e2m1" if DTYPE == "fp4" else "e4m3"
+            k = tl.arange(0, WIDTH)
+            q = tl.load(Q.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8)) + query[:, None] * Q_ROW + head[:, None] * Q_HEAD + k[None, :], query_valid[:, None], other=0)
+            key = tl.load(CACHE + page_base[None, :] + slot[None, :] * WIDTH + k[:, None], pool_valid[None, :], other=0)
+            if DTYPE == "fp8":
+                key = key.to(tl.float8e4nv, bitcast=True)
+                q = q.to(tl.float8e4nv, bitcast=True)
+            group = tl.arange(0, 4)
+            if QSCALE is None:
+                qs = tl.full((QUERY_TILE * 32, 4), 127, tl.uint8)
+            else:
+                scale_base = QSCALE.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8))
+                qs = tl.load(
+                    scale_base + query[:, None] * QS_ROW + head[:, None] * QS_HEAD + group[None, :],
+                    query_valid[:, None],
+                    other=127,
+                )
+            ks = tl.load(
+                CACHE + page_base[:, None] + PAGE_SIZE * WIDTH + slot[:, None] * 4 + group[None, :],
+                pool_valid[:, None],
+                other=127,
+            )
+            dots = tl.dot_scaled(key.T, ks, FORMAT, q.T, qs, FORMAT)
+        else:
+            k = tl.arange(0, 128)
+            q = tl.load(Q + query[:, None] * Q_ROW + head[:, None] * Q_HEAD + k[None, :], query_valid[:, None], other=0.0)
+            if DTYPE == "fp8":
+                pointer = CACHE.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.float8e4nv)) + page_base[None, :] + slot[None, :] * 128 + k[:, None]
+            else:
+                pointer = CACHE.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.bfloat16)) + page_base[None, :] // 2 + slot[None, :] * 128 + k[:, None]
+            key = tl.load(pointer, pool_valid[None, :], other=0.0)
+            dots = tl.dot(key.T, q.T)
+        weights = tl.load(WEIGHTS + query * W_ROW + head, query_valid, other=0)
+        if DTYPE == "fp8" and FP8_SCALE_FORMAT == "fp32":
+            scale_ptr = (CACHE + page_base + PAGE_SIZE * 128 + slot * 4).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.float32))
+            scales = tl.load(scale_ptr, pool_valid, other=1)
+            if BF16_REDUCTION:
+                dots *= scales[:, None]
+        if BF16_REDUCTION:
+            # Match SM100 DeepGEMM: four BF16 FMA chains, then two BF16 adds.
+            positive = tl.maximum(dots, 0).to(tl.bfloat16).reshape((POOL_TILE, QUERY_TILE, 32))
+            head_weights = tl.broadcast_to(weights[None, :], (POOL_TILE, QUERY_TILE * 32)).reshape((POOL_TILE, QUERY_TILE, 32))
+            sums = tl.full((POOL_TILE, QUERY_TILE, 4), 0, tl.bfloat16)
+            for i in tl.static_range(8):
+                indices = tl.broadcast_to((4 * i + tl.arange(0, 4))[None, None, :], (POOL_TILE, QUERY_TILE, 4))
+                values = tl.gather(positive, indices, axis=2)
+                ws = tl.gather(head_weights, indices, axis=2)
+                sums = tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+                    "fma.rn.bf16 $0, $1, $2, $3;", constraints="=h,h,h,h", args=[values, ws, sums], dtype=tl.bfloat16, is_pure=True, pack=1
+                )
+            low = tl.broadcast_to(tl.arange(0, 2)[None, None, :], (POOL_TILE, QUERY_TILE, 2))
+            pairs = (tl.gather(sums, low, axis=2).to(tl.float32) + tl.gather(sums, low + 2, axis=2).to(tl.float32)).to(tl.bfloat16)
+            scores = tl.sum(pairs.to(tl.float32), axis=2).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32).T
+        else:
+            per_head = tl.maximum(dots, 0) * weights[None, :]
+            scores = tl.sum(per_head.reshape((POOL_TILE, QUERY_TILE, 32)), axis=2).T
+            if DTYPE == "fp8" and FP8_SCALE_FORMAT == "fp32":
+                scores *= scales[None, :]
+        row = query_start + tl.arange(0, QUERY_TILE)
+        valid_row = (row >= 0) & (row < end) & (row < N_QUERY)
+        position = tl.load(POSITIONS + row * POS_STRIDE, valid_row, other=-1).to(tl.int64)
+        lengths = tl.where((position >= 0) & (position < 2147483647), tl.minimum((position + 1) // POOL_SIZE, SCORE_COLS), 0)
+        valid = pool_valid[None, :] & (pool[None, :] < lengths[:, None])
+        scores = tl.where(valid, scores, -float("inf"))
+        tl.store(SCORES + row[:, None] * SCORE_ROW + pool[None, :], scores, valid_row[:, None] & (pool[None, :] < SCORE_COLS))

+    out = torch.full(output_shape, -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    topk = ids.shape[1] * pool_size

+            continue
+        length = position + 1

+            out[row, :length] = torch.arange(length)
+            continue

+        for i, pool in enumerate(ids[src].tolist()):

+    if dtype == "bf16":

+    if dtype == "fp8":

+        return (value.float() / scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8), scale.reshape(1).view(torch.uint8)
+    blocks = value.float().reshape(4, 32)
+    exponent = (blocks.abs().amax(-1).clamp_min(6 * 2**-126) / 6).log2().ceil()

+def _native_head_reduction(dots, weights):
+    """BF16 FMA chains in SM100 DeepGEMM head order, using exact FP64 products."""
+    positive = dots.relu().bfloat16().double()
+    sums = torch.zeros(4, dots.shape[1], device=dots.device, dtype=torch.float64)
+    for head in range(32):
+        lane = head % 4
+        sums[lane] = (positive[head] * weights[head].double() + sums[lane]).bfloat16().double()
+    pairs = (sums[:2] + sums[2:]).bfloat16().double()
+    return (pairs[0] + pairs[1]).bfloat16().double()
